findings.result: The exact-range entry e-process is mathematically valid under the stated finite-support/predictable-proposal assumptions. For A~q_t and Y|A=i with mean p_i, H_t(q_j)=W_A^2 Y/[q_t(A)q_j(A)] has conditional mean sum_i W_i^2 p_i/q_j(i). Therefore G_t(j)=H_t(W)-H_t(q_j) has conditional mean S_t(W)-S_t(q_j). The stated R_t(j)=max_i |W_i^2/q_t(i)*(1/W_i-1/q_j(i))| bounds |G_t(j)| because Y is in {0,1}. Under the no-improvement null E[G_t|F_{t-1}]<=0, Z_t=G_t/R_t lies in [-1,1], so for any predictable lambda in [0,1], 1+lambda Z_t is nonnegative with conditional mean <=1; the product is a nonnegative supermartingale.

The source's Bonferroni threshold 80 is exactly consistent with four non-base candidates and familywise entry delta 0.05: per-candidate alpha=0.0125 and e-value/Ville threshold 1/0.0125=80. Selection of the largest already-certified candidate does not invalidate the union bound over the four fixed candidate nulls.

The harm process construction is structurally compatible with the published e-detector framework. With D_t=H_t(q_active)-H_t(W) and an exact predictable range, L_t=1+lambda D_t/R_t is a conditional e-value under no-harm when lambda is predictable in [0,1]. Shin-Ramdas-Rinaldo define baseline CUSUM e-detectors recursively as M_n=L_n max(M_{n-1},1), and their Theorem 2.4/Definition 2.12 make threshold 1/alpha a valid (possibly conservative) ARL-control choice. Thus alpha_harm=0.001 -> threshold 1000 is theoretically supported for the detector's no-harm ARL semantics, not for global probability-of-ever-false-fallback.

A separate deterministic four-branch transcription check reproduces the one-step supermartingale inequality without using worker code. Using W=(0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4), p=(0.02,0.01,0.03,0.005), q_t=(0.25,0.25,0.25,0.25), q_j=(0.05,0.15,0.30,0.50): S_base=0.015, S_j=0.0172666666667, E[G]=-0.00226666666667, R=0.4, and E[1+Z]=0.994333333333<=1 for lambda=1. Branchwise normalized gain when Y=1 is (-1,-2/3,0,0.8), within [-1,1].

The source aggregate arithmetic is internally consistent: 199.6/214.25387=0.9316051094 (reported 0.93161), 199.6/199.45836=1.0007101232 (reported 1.00071), and the fallback recovers 214.25387-199.45836=14.79551 variance units (reported about 14.80). The entry-only loss versus base is about 6.8395%, matching the stated about 6.8%.

The headline synthetic numbers are not exact-replay ready. The certificate does not persist the simulation program, RNG seed(s), the definition or realized values of z_i, the realized proxy-noise vector, raw replicate-level outputs, or a machine-readable trajectory/run bundle. The certificate-creation commit adds the JSON certificate itself; no source-matched executable or raw run artifact was found in the audited path/commit. Consequently the 500-replicate abrupt metrics, 200-per-threshold tradeoff, and 300-replicate gradual-drift metrics are source-run engineering evidence rather than independently reproduced results.

No protocol-matched public independent reproduction of the combined adaptive-importance-sampling entry gate plus e-CUSUM fallback was found in this audit. The public papers support ingredients (time-uniform/betting inference and e-detector ARL control), not this exact composed mechanism or its reported synthetic performance.

The source correctly limits its formal claim. The entry wealth certifies a historical/average conditional gain, not current post-drift gain; e-CUSUM supplies ARL rather than global false-alarm probability; false fallback is validity-neutral only because fallback returns to the support-preserving unbiased base proposal; and none of the synthetic evidence establishes LLM-agent, tool-environment, correlated-resampling or AGI capability gains.

The empirical-Bernstein gate mentioned in the source is a proposed next step, not the mechanism used in the reported synthetic run. The reported run used an equal mixture of fixed betting strengths lambda in {0.25,0.5,0.75,1.0}. Do not attribute the reported switch/fallback numbers to a Howard-style variance-adaptive empirical-Bernstein implementation.
